seo.metaDescription: SASSA status shows 'Referred'? Learn what this fraud flag means, why applications get referred for investigation, and step-by-step instructions to clear your name and get your grant.

contentBlocks.title: Referred — How to Resolve a Fraud Flag
contentBlocks.description: Your SASSA status shows 'Referred' — your application has been flagged for investigation. Understand why applications are referred, what this means for your grant, and the exact steps to clear your name and get your application moving again.

contentBlocks.text: The 'Referred' status is a serious flag. It means SASSA's fraud detection system identified something unusual about your application and has sent it for manual investigation. This is an administrative hold, not a criminal accusation, but it must be resolved before your grant can proceed.
This status affects applicants whose grant applications have been flagged for additional manual review by a senior SASSA officer.

contentBlocks.title: Manual Review Required
contentBlocks.text: A senior SASSA officer is reviewing your application manually. This may take additional time. You do not need to take any action unless contacted.

contentBlocks.explanation: SASSA's automated fraud detection system flagged your application for suspicious activity. Your file has been 'referred' to a human investigator for manual review.
whyItHappens: Your ID number was used in multiple applications
Your phone number is registered under a different name
Your bank account is linked to multiple SASSA applicants
Suspicious activity was detected on your account (multiple logins, unusual pattern)
Your application matches a known fraud pattern in SASSA's system
contentBlocks.howLongItLasts: This is a serious block that can remain active for weeks or months until the fraud investigation is completed. The timeline depends on the complexity of your case.
whatYouShouldDo: Contact the SASSA Fraud Hotline on 0800 60 10 11 to understand why you were flagged
Prepare to visit your nearest SASSA office with certified copies of your ID, proof of address, and recent bank statements
Bring any documents that prove your identity and that you are the legitimate applicant
Cooperate fully with the investigation — providing false information will make the situation worse

faqs.question: Does 'Referred' mean I will be arrested?
faqs.answer: No. It is a precautionary administrative lock to prevent unauthorized grant payouts. Once you verify your identity in person, the lock is typically lifted.

faqs.question: How long does the 'Referred' investigation take?
faqs.answer: It varies. Simple cases may be resolved in 2 to 4 weeks, while complex investigations can take several months.

faqs.question: Can I appeal a 'Referred' status?
faqs.answer: This is not an appeal situation. You need to resolve the fraud flag by providing verification documents to SASSA. Contact the Fraud Hotline for specific guidance.

faqs.question: What if someone else used my ID to apply for a grant?
faqs.answer: Inform SASSA immediately. You will need to file an affidavit at a police station and provide it to SASSA to clear your name.
